data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A recursive construction based on odd-even merge sort (Batcher's) can be optimized by pruning redundant comparators specific to n=13 to reach a 45-comparator network, but this method cannot reach 44.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Greedy removal might get stuck at 46 or 47 because the order of removal matters, and a different combination of removals might yield 45.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"There might be no 45-comparator network reachable by simply removing comparators from Batcher's construction; structural changes might be needed.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"This method is fundamentally limited by the starting point (Batcher's) and is unlikely to reach 44 if Batcher's is far from the optimal structure.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Start with Batcher's odd-even merge for n=13 (48 comparators). Identify comparators that are redundant for all 8192 binary vectors by testing removal one by one. If removing a comparator still sorts all vectors, remove it permanently. Continue until no more can be removed. This yields a structurally understood, verified network.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
